question: How many S1 integration failures are recovered by merging the agents' existing patches better?
decision_rule: Primary metric: the share of the 134 features labeled integration in the S1 main run that pass after the llm re-merge. At 50% or more, integration failures are mostly mechanical merge conflicts: S2 adds automatic merging to the coop baseline and targets the failures that remain. Below 50%, the conflicts need more than a merge tool, and S2 tests process interventions against integration (one agent owns the merge, interface agreement). Union is reported as a no-model baseline. Regressions (features the official score passed that the re-merge fails) are reported for both methods.

methods.union: keep both sides of every conflict block, agent 2's lines first (git's union merge)
methods.llm: gpt-6-luna resolves the conflict blocks of each file in one call; it sees only the file path and the code around the conflicts, not the feature descriptions or tests; single attempt, no repair loop

dev.note: screening runs; used to check the pipeline and the prompt, which may change here

test.note: all S1 main coop runs whose naive merge conflicted; run once with the frozen prompt
